**Özet:**

1. **5 UDP portu** eklendi (14550–14554); her cihaz farklı porta bağlanabilir.
2. **QGC bağlantı bilgisi** arayüze eklendi: IP, port ve güvenlik duvarı uyarısı.
3. **`docker-compose.yml`** güncellendi: tüm portlar `udpin` (sunucu modu) ile dinleniyor; telefon QGC bu portlara bağlanabilir.

**QGC telefon bağlantısı:**
- QGC → Bağlantı Ekle → UDP
- IP: Bilgisayarınızın IP’si (panelde gösterilir)
- Port: 14550 (veya 14551, 14552…)
- Telefon ve bilgisayar aynı Wi‑Fi ağında olmalı
- Windows Güvenlik Duvarı’nda UDP 14550–14554 portlarına izin verin

**Sonraki adımlar:**
1. `python main.py` ile paneli çalıştırın, “Ayarları Kaydet ve Başlat”a tıklayın.
2. Windows Güvenlik Duvarı’nda gerekirse kural ekleyin: `netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="ArduPilot SITL" dir=in action=allow protocol=UDP localport=14550-14554`
3. Bağlantı yoksa Docker’ın `network_mode: host` kullanıp kullanmadığını kontrol edin.

**Yapılan değişiklikler:**

1. **Docker portları** – `0.0.0.0` ile tüm ağ arayüzlerine bağlandı.
2. **`firewall-acik.bat`** – UDP 14540–14554 portlarını açan betik eklendi.
3. **Arayüz** – Bağlantı sorununda firewall betiğini çalıştırma talimatı eklendi.

**Bağlantı için adımlar:**

1. `firewall-acik.bat` dosyasına sağ tık → **Yönetici olarak çalıştır**
2. Paneldeki IP’yi kontrol et (192.168.1.104 bilgisayarın IP’si olmalı)
3. Docker container’ı yeniden başlat: panelden "Tümünü Durdur" → "Sistemi Başlat"
4. QGC’de: Bağlantı Ekle → UDP → IP: `192.168.1.104`, Port: `14550`

**Hâlâ bağlanmıyorsa:**

- `ipconfig` ile bilgisayarın IP’sini doğrula (192.168.1.x)
- Telefon ve bilgisayarın aynı Wi‑Fi ağında olduğundan emin ol
- QGC’de bağlantı tipi olarak **UDP** seçildiğinden emin ol (TCP değil)
- Docker Desktop’ın çalıştığını kontrol et

[Startup Options — MAVProxy  documentation](https://ardupilot.org/mavproxy/docs/getting_started/starting.html)<br/><br/># MAVProxy Docker with UDP Relay for ArduPilot SITL<br/><br/>## Containerized MAVProxy<br/><br/>There is a containerized MAVProxy project available that provides Docker support for MAVProxy, complete with a Dockerfile and docker-compose configuration.[1] This enables running MAVProxy in a container environment.<br/><br/>## UDP Relay and Forwarding<br/><br/>MAVProxy supports telemetry forwarding over UDP to enable communication between SITL simulations and ground stations.[3] The `--out` parameter allows forwarding MAVLink packets to network addresses, for example:<br/><br/>```<br/>mavproxy.py --out 127.0.0.1:14550<br/>```<br/><br/>This forwards data to local or remote ground station software.[3][5]<br/><br/>## ArduPilot UDP Proxy Alternative<br/><br/>For more advanced relay requirements, ArduPilot provides UDPProxy—a dedicated UDP/TCP/WebSocket proxy for MAVLink that facilitates communication between multiple parties.[2] It supports:<br/>- UDP, TCP, and WebSocket connections<br/>- MAVLink2 signed authentication<br/>- Both IPv4 connections for users and support engineers<br/>- Mixed connection types[2]<br/><br/>## SITL Integration<br/><br/>MAVProxy is the primary tool for ArduPilot SITL testing and supports direct integration with SITL simulators.[4] It can connect to SITL via UDP on localhost (typically port 14550) and forward telemetry to multiple ground stations simultaneously.[3][4] |

[History](https://ardupilot.org/mavproxy/docs/common-history-of-ardupilot.html)\n\n# Telemetry Forwarding¶\n\nA key feature of MAVProxy is its ability to forward the messages from your UAV over the network via UDP to multiple other ground station software on other devices. For example: you can run a ground station on a laptop next to your antenna and forward via wifi to a smartphone/tablet which lets you easily relocate to launch into wind before heading back to your fixed antenna. You can also use it to send telemetry data to a friend acting as spotter several kilometers away (via 4G vpn) during a longer flight so that he could monitor the entire flight and determine where to look to find the aircraft in flight.\n\nTo forward the MAVLink data over the network including to a local program on your PC you simply need to add some extra parameters when starting MAVProxy via the command line.\n\n## Local Forwarding¶\n\nTo connect with a local ground station software (such as Mission Planner or QGC) start MAVProxy under Linux with the command:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmavproxy.py --master=/dev/ttyACM0 --baudrate 115200 --out 127.0.0.1:14550\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nan abbreviated version also works:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmavproxy.py --out 127.0.0.1:14550\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nsince MAVProxy will auto-connect to the autopilot on the Linux PC.\n\nFor a Windows PC, start a command prompt and enter:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmavproxy --master=COMx --out 127.0.0.1:14550\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nwhere COMx is the com port to which the autopilot is attached.\n\nThen open the ground station software and select a UDP connection on port 14550. It should then connect to your UAV.\n\n## Forwarding to Remotes¶\n\nNote\n\nWhile MAVProxy also has the capability of forwarding using TCP, it is not recommended, since network delays can cause long lags if joystick control is being used.\n\nFinally, you can add the IP address of any computer to forward the telemetry stream onwards to other ground stations.\n\nOn the local network/wifi you will need to ensure there is no firewall on the client PC stopping the incoming stream to your ground station software.\n\nAdd - -out destination IP address:14550 to the end of the MAVProxy command. You can add as many separate - -out parameters as you want depending on how many extra ground stations you are running.\n\nSet each ground station to listen for UDP packets on port 14550 and, again, make sure its firewall is not blocking incoming traffic on UDP port 14550."
}

  "markdown": "# radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker\n\nDocker container for ArduPilot Software-in-the-Loop Simulator\n\n⭐ 65 stars | 🍴 47 forks\n\n## Links\n\n- [Repository](https://github.com/radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker)\n- [Issues](https://github.com/radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker/issues)\n- [Pull Requests](https://github.com/radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker/pulls)\n\n## Files\n\n- [.github/workflows/](https://github.com/radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker/tree/master/.github/workflows)\n- [Dockerfile](https://github.com/radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker/blob/master/Dockerfile)\n- [LICENSE.md](https://github.com/radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker/blob/master/LICENSE.md)\n- [README.md](https://github.com/radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker/blob/master/README.md)\n- [env.list](https://github.com/radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker/blob/master/env.list)\n\n## README\n\n# ArduPilot Software-in-the-Loop Simulator Docker Container\n\nThe purpose of this is to run an ArduPilot SITL from within Docker.\n\n## DockerHub\n\nA pre-built Docker image is available on DockerHub at:\n\n[https://hub.docker.com/r/radarku/ardupilot-sitl](https://hub.docker.com/r/radarku/ardupilot-sitl)\n\n- To download it, run &#96;docker pull radarku/ardupilot-sitl&#96;\n\n- To run it, run &#96;docker run -it --rm -p 5760:5760 radarku/ardupilot-sitl&#96;\n\n- To use it with [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/), add the following service to your &#96;docker-compose.yml&#96; file:\n\nYou can launch it with &#96;docker-compose up -d&#96;\nIf you update your &#96;docker-compose.yml&#96;, you can restart your container by running &#96;docker-compose up -d&#96; without getting the container ID and killing the container manually. See [#3](https://github.com/radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker/issues/3)\nTo check the logs in &#96;ArduCopter.log&#96;, run &#96;docker exec -it \"$FOLDER_NAME_ardupilot-sitl_1\" watch -n 1 \"cat /tmp/ArduCopter.log\"&#96;, where you should update &#96;$FOLDER_NAME&#96; with the folder containing the &#96;docker-compose.yml&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;yaml\nservices:\nardupilot-sitl:\nimage: radarku/ardupilot-sitl\nplatform: linux/amd64\ntty: true\nports:\n- 5760:5760\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Quick Start\n\nIf you'd rather build the docker image yourself:\n\n&#96;docker build --tag ardupilot github.com/radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker&#96;\n\nYou can now use the &#96;--build-arg&#96; option to specify which branch or tag in the ardupilot\nrepository you'd like to use. Here's an example:\n\n&#96;docker build --tag ardupilot --build-arg COPTER_TAG=Copter-4.0.1 github.com/radarku/ardupilot-sitl-docker&#96;\n\nIf no COPTER_TAG is supplied, the build will use the default defined in the Dockerfile, currently set at Copter-4.0.3\n\nTo run the image:\n\n&#96;docker run -it --rm -p 5760:5760 ardupilot&#96;\n\nThis will start an ArduCopter SITL on host TCP port 5760, so to connect to it from the host, you could:\n\n&#96;mavproxy.py --master=tcp:localhost:5760&#96;\n\n## Options\n\nThere are a number of options available to configure the simulator, for example, to run an ArduRover instance on port 5761, you could:\n\n&#96;docker run -it --rm -p 5761:5760 --env VEHICLE=APMrover2 ardupilot&#96;\n\nWe also have an example &#96;env.list&#96; file which can help you maintain your options and called like so:\n\n&#96;docker run -it --rm -p 5761:5760 --env-file env.list ardupilot&#96;\n\nThe full list of options and their default values is:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nINSTANCE    0\nLAT         42.3898\nLON         -71.1476\nALT         14\nDIR         270\nMODEL       +\nSPEEDUP     1\nVEHICLE     arducopter\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSo, for example, you could issue a command such as:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ndocker run -it --rm -p 5761:5760 \\\n--env VEHICLE=APMrover2 \\\n--env MODEL=rover-skid \\\n--env LAT=39.9656 \\\n--env LON=-75.1810 \\\n--env ALT=276 \\\n--env DIR=180 \\\n--env SPEEDUP=2 \\\nardupilot\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nVehicles and their corresponding models are listed below:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nArduCopter: octa-quad|tri|singlecopter|firefly|gazebo-\niris|calibration|hexa|heli|+|heli-compound|dodeca-\nhexa|heli-dual|coaxcopter|X|quad|y6|IrisRos|octa\nAPMRover2: rover|gazebo-rover|rover-skid|calibration\nArduSub: vectored\nArduPlane: gazebo-zephyr|CRRCSim|last_letter|plane-\nvtail|plane|quadplane-tilttri|quadplane|quadplane-\ntilttrivec|calibration|plane-elevon|plane-\ntailsitter|plane-dspoilers|quadplane-tri\n|quadplane-cl84|jsbsim\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;"
}

**Özet**

MAVProxy relay eklendi. Akış:

```
SITL → udp:mavproxy:14560 → MAVProxy → udpin:14550 (QGC bağlanır)
```

**Yapılanlar:**
1. **MAVProxy container** – SITL’den gelen trafiği alıp 14550–14554 portlarına yönlendiriyor
2. **SITL** – Sadece MAVProxy’ye (14560) ve web panele (14540) bağlanıyor
3. **`generate_yaml_content`** – Yeni yapıya göre güncellendi

**Kullanım:**
1. Panelden "Tümünü Durdur" → "Ayarları Kaydet ve Başlat"
2. QGC: UDP → IP: `192.168.1.104`, Port: `14550`

**Sonraki adımlar:**
- Bağlantı yoksa `docker-compose logs mavproxy` ile MAVProxy loglarını kontrol et
- `radarku/ardupilot-sitl` imajında `mavproxy.py` yoksa, MAVProxy’yi ayrı bir imajla çalıştırmayı dene

**Özet**

Tüm yönetim `main.py` üzerinden yapılıyor:

1. **config.json** – Ayarlar burada saklanıyor.
2. **docker-compose.yml** – Her başlatma/kaydetme sırasında `main.py` tarafından oluşturuluyor.
3. **Sistemi Başlat** – `config.json` okunuyor, compose üretiliyor, ardından `docker-compose up` çalışıyor.
4. **Ayarları Kaydet ve Başlat** – Form verisi `config.json`’a yazılıyor, compose üretiliyor, servisler yeniden başlatılıyor.
5. **Sayfa yükleme** – `/api/config` ile kayıtlı ayarlar forma yükleniyor.

**Akış:**
- İlk açılış: Varsayılan ayarlar kullanılır.
- "Sistemi Başlat": `config.json` varsa ondan, yoksa varsayılanlardan compose üretilir.
- "Ayarları Kaydet ve Başlat": Form verisi kaydedilir ve compose yeniden üretilir.

**Sonraki adımlar:**
- `docker-compose.yml` ve `config.json` için `.gitignore` eklenebilir.
- Ayarların geçerliliğini kontrol eden bir doğrulama eklenebilir.

  "markdown": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\n\"\"\"\nFramework to start a simulated vehicle and connect it to MAVProxy.\n\nPeter Barker, April 2016\nbased on sim_vehicle.sh by Andrew Tridgell, October 2011\n\nAP_FLAKE8_CLEAN\n\n\"\"\"\n\nimport atexit\nimport datetime\nimport errno\nimport optparse\nimport os\nimport os.path\nimport re\nimport signal\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\nimport textwrap\nimport time\nimport shlex\nimport binascii\nimport math\n\nfrom pysim import util\nfrom pysim import vehicleinfo\n\n\n# List of open terminal windows for macosx\nwindowID = []\n\nautotest_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))\nroot_dir = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(autotest_dir, '../..'))\n\ntry:\n from pymavlink import mavextra\nexcept ImportError:\n sys.path.append(os.path.join(root_dir, \"modules/mavlink\"))\n from pymavlink import mavextra\n\nos.environ[\"SIM_VEHICLE_SESSION\"] = binascii.hexlify(os.urandom(8)).decode()\n\n\nclass CompatError(Exception):\n \"\"\"A custom exception class to hold state if we encounter the parse\n error we are looking for\"\"\"\n def __init__(self, error, opts, rargs):\n Exception.__init__(self, error)\n self.opts = opts\n self.rargs = rargs\n\n\nclass CompatOptionParser(optparse.OptionParser):\n \"\"\"An option parser which emulates the behaviour of the old\n sim_vehicle.sh; if passed -C, the first argument not understood starts\n a list of arguments that are passed straight to mavproxy\n \"\"\"\n\n class CustomFormatter(optparse.IndentedHelpFormatter):\n def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):\n optparse.IndentedHelpFormatter.__init__(self, *args, **kwargs)\n\n # taken and modified from from optparse.py's format_option\n def format_option_preserve_nl(self, option):\n # The help for each option consists of two parts:\n # * the opt strings and metavars\n # eg. (\"-x\", or \"-fFILENAME, --file=FILENAME\")\n # * the user-supplied help string\n # eg. (\"turn on expert mode\", \"read data from FILENAME\")\n #\n # If possible, we write both of these on the same line:\n # -x turn on expert mode\n #\n # But if the opt string list is too long, we put the help\n # string on a second line, indented to the same column it would\n # start in if it fit on the first line.\n # -fFILENAME, --file=FILENAME\n # read data from FILENAME\n result = []\n opts = self.option_strings[option]\n opt_width = self.help_position - self.current_indent - 2\n if len(opts) &gt; opt_width:\n opts = \"%*s%s\\n\" % (self.current_indent, \"\", opts)\n else: # start help on same line as opts\n opts = \"%*s%-*s \" % (self.current_indent, \"\", opt_width, opts)\n result.append(opts)\n if option.help:\n help_text = self.expand_default(option)\n tw = textwrap.TextWrapper(replace_whitespace=False,\n initial_indent=\"\",\n subsequent_indent=\" \",\n width=self.help_width)\n\n for line in help_text.split(\"\\n\"):\n help_lines = tw.wrap(line)\n for wline in help_lines:\n result.extend([\"%*s%s\\n\" % (self.help_position,\n \"\",\n wline)])\n elif opts[-1] != \"\\n\":\n result.append(\"\\n\")\n return \"\".join(result)\n\n def format_option(self, option):\n if str(option).find('frame') != -1:\n return self.format_option_preserve_nl(option)\n return optparse.IndentedHelpFormatter.format_option(self, option)\n\n def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):\n formatter = CompatOptionParser.CustomFormatter()\n optparse.OptionParser.__init__(self,\n *args,\n formatter=formatter,\n **kwargs)\n\n def error(self, error):\n \"\"\"Override default error handler called by\n optparse.OptionParser.parse_args when a parse error occurs;\n raise a detailed exception which can be caught\n \"\"\"\n if error.find(\"no such option\") != -1:\n raise CompatError(error, self.values, self.rargs)\n\n optparse.OptionParser.error(self, error)\n\n def parse_args(self, args=None, values=None):\n '''Wrap parse_args so we can catch the exception raised upon\n discovering the known parameter parsing error\n '''\n\n try:\n opts, args = optparse.OptionParser.parse_args(self)\n except CompatError as e:\n if not e.opts.sim_vehicle_sh_compatible:\n print(e)\n print(\"Perhaps you want --sim_vehicle_sh_compatible (-C)?\")\n sys.exit(1)\n if e.opts.mavproxy_args:\n print(\"--mavproxy-args not permitted in compat mode\")\n sys.exit(1)\n\n args = []\n opts = e.opts\n mavproxy_args = [str(e)[16:]] # this trims \"no such option\" off\n mavproxy_args.extend(e.rargs)\n opts.ensure_value(\"mavproxy_args\", \" \".join(mavproxy_args))\n\n return opts, args\n\n\ndef cygwin_pidof(proc_name):\n \"\"\" Thanks to kata198 for this:\n https://github.com/kata198/cygwin-ps-misc/blob/master/pidof\n \"\"\"\n pipe = subprocess.Popen(\"ps -ea | grep \" + proc_name,\n shell=True,\n stdout=subprocess.PIPE)\n output_lines = pipe.stdout.read().decode('utf-8').replace(\"\\r\", \"\").split(\"\\n\")\n ret = pipe.wait()\n pids = []\n if ret != 0:\n # No results\n return []\n for line in output_lines:\n if not line:\n continue\n line_split = [item for item in line.split(' ') if item]\n cmd = line_split[-1].split('/')[-1]\n if cmd == proc_name:\n try:\n pid = int(line_split[0].strip())\n except Exception:\n pid = int(line_split[1].strip())\n if pid not in pids:\n pids.append(pid)\n return pids\n\n\ndef under_cygwin():\n \"\"\"Return if Cygwin binary exist\"\"\"\n return os.path.exists(\"/usr/bin/cygstart\")\n\n\ndef under_macos():\n return sys.platform == 'darwin'\n\n\ndef under_vagrant():\n return os.path.isdir(\"/vagrant\")\n\n\ndef under_wsl2():\n import platform\n return 'microsoft-standard-WSL2' in platform.release()\n\n\ndef wsl2_host_ip():\n if not under_wsl2() or cmd_opts.no_wsl2_network:\n return None\n\n pipe = subprocess.Popen(\"ip route show default | awk '{print $3}'\",\n shell=True,\n stdout=subprocess.PIPE)\n output_lines = pipe.stdout.read().decode('utf-8').strip(' \\r\\n')\n ret = pipe.wait()\n\n if ret != 0:\n # Command exited with an error. The output it generated probably isn't what we're expecting\n return None\n\n if not output_lines:\n # No output detected, maybe there's no nameserver or WSL2 has some abnormal firewalls/network settings?\n return None\n\n return str(output_lines)\n\n\ndef kill_tasks_cygwin(victims):\n \"\"\"Shell out to ps -ea to find processes to kill\"\"\"\n for victim in list(victims):\n pids = cygwin_pidof(victim)\n# progress(\"pids for (%s): %s\" %\n# (victim,\",\".join([ str(p) for p in pids])))\n for apid in pids:\n os.kill(apid, signal.SIGKILL)\n\n\ndef kill_tasks_macos():\n for window in windowID:\n cmd = (\"osascript -e \\'tell application \\\"Terminal\\\" to close \"\n \"(window(get index of window id %s))\\'\" % window)\n os.system(cmd)\n\n\ndef kill_tasks_psutil(victims):\n \"\"\"Use the psutil module to kill tasks by name. Sadly, this module is\n not available on Windows, but when it is we should be able to *just*\n use this routine\"\"\"\n import psutil\n for proc in psutil.process_iter():\n pdict = proc.as_dict(attrs=['environ', 'status'])\n if pdict['status'] == psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE:\n continue\n if pdict['environ'] is not None:\n if pdict['environ'].get('SIM_VEHICLE_SESSION') == os.environ['SIM_VEHICLE_SESSION']:\n proc.kill()\n\n\ndef kill_tasks_pkill(victims):\n \"\"\"Shell out to pkill(1) to kill processed by name\"\"\"\n for victim in victims: # pkill takes a single pattern, so iterate\n cmd = [\"pkill\", victim[:15]] # pkill matches only first 15 characters\n run_cmd_blocking(\"pkill\", cmd, quiet=True)\n\n\ndef kill_tasks():\n \"\"\"Clean up stray processes by name. This is a shotgun approach\"\"\"\n progress(\"Killing tasks\")\n\n if cmd_opts.coverage:\n import psutil\n for proc in psutil.process_iter(['pid', 'name', 'environ']):\n if proc.name() not in [\"arducopter\", \"ardurover\", \"arduplane\", \"ardusub\", \"antennatracker\"]:\n # only kill vehicle that way\n continue\n if os.environ['SIM_VEHICLE_SESSION'] not in proc.environ().get('SIM_VEHICLE_SESSION'):\n # only kill vehicle launched with sim_vehicle.py that way\n continue\n proc.terminate()\n progress(\"Waiting SITL to exit cleanly and write coverage .gcda\")\n try:\n proc.wait(timeout=30)\n progress(\"Done\")\n except psutil.TimeoutExpired:\n progress(\"SITL doesn't want to exit cleaning, killing ...\")\n proc.kill()\n\n try:\n victim_names = {\n 'JSBSim',\n 'lt-JSBSim',\n 'ArduPlane.elf',\n 'ArduCopter.elf',\n 'ArduSub.elf',\n 'Rover.elf',\n 'AntennaTracker.elf',\n 'JSBSIm.exe',\n 'MAVProxy.exe',\n 'runsim.py',\n 'AntennaTracker.elf',\n 'scrimmage',\n 'ardurover',\n 'arduplane',\n 'arducopter'\n }\n for vehicle in vinfo.options:\n for frame in vinfo.options[vehicle][\"frames\"]:\n frame_info = vinfo.options[vehicle][\"frames\"][frame]\n if \"waf_target\" not in frame_info:\n continue\n exe_name = os.path.basename(frame_info[\"waf_target\"])\n victim_names.add(exe_name)\n\n if under_cygwin():\n return kill_tasks_cygwin(victim_names)\n if under_macos() and os.environ.get('DISPLAY'):\n # use special macos kill routine if Display is on\n return kill_tasks_macos()\n\n try:\n kill_tasks_psutil(victim_names)\n except ImportError:\n kill_tasks_pkill(victim_names)\n except Exception as e:\n progress(\"kill_tasks failed: {}\".format(str(e)))\n\n\ndef progress(text):\n \"\"\"Display sim_vehicle progress text\"\"\"\n print(\"SIM_VEHICLE: \" + text)\n\n\ndef wait_unlimited():\n \"\"\"Wait until signal received\"\"\"\n while True:\n time.sleep(600)\n\n\nvinfo = vehicleinfo.VehicleInfo()\n\n\ndef do_build(opts, frame_options):\n \"\"\"Build sitl using waf\"\"\"\n progress(\"WAF build\")\n\n old_dir = os.getcwd()\n os.chdir(root_dir)\n\n waf_light = os.path.join(root_dir, \"modules/waf/waf-light\")\n\n configure_target = frame_options.get('configure_target', 'sitl')\n\n cmd_configure = [waf_light, \"configure\", \"--board\", configure_target]\n if opts.debug:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--debug\")\n\n if opts.coverage:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--coverage\")\n\n if opts.enable_onvif and 'antennatracker' in frame_options[\"waf_target\"]:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--enable-onvif\")\n\n if opts.OSD:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--enable-sfml\")\n cmd_configure.append(\"--sitl-osd\")\n\n if opts.OSDMSP:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--osd\")\n\n if opts.rgbled:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--enable-sfml\")\n cmd_configure.append(\"--sitl-rgbled\")\n\n if opts.tonealarm:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--enable-sfml-audio\")\n\n if opts.math_check_indexes:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--enable-math-check-indexes\")\n\n if opts.enable_ekf2:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--enable-EKF2\")\n\n if opts.disable_ekf3:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--disable-EKF3\")\n\n if opts.postype_single:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--postype-single\")\n\n if opts.ekf_double:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--ekf-double\")\n\n if opts.ekf_single:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--ekf-single\")\n\n if opts.force_32bit:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--force-32bit\")\n\n if opts.ubsan:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--ubsan\")\n\n if opts.ubsan_abort:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--ubsan-abort\")\n\n if opts.num_aux_imus:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--num-aux-imus=%s\" % opts.num_aux_imus)\n\n for nv in opts.define:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--define=%s\" % nv)\n\n if opts.enable_DDS:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--enable-DDS\")\n\n if opts.disable_networking:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--disable-networking\")\n\n if opts.enable_ppp:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--enable-PPP\")\n\n if opts.enable_networking_tests:\n cmd_configure.append(\"--enable-networking-tests\")\n\n pieces = [shlex.split(x) for x in opts.waf_configure_args]\n for piece in pieces:\n cmd_configure.extend(piece)\n\n if not cmd_opts.no_configure:\n run_cmd_blocking(\"Configure waf\", cmd_configure, check=True)\n\n if opts.clean:\n run_cmd_blocking(\"Building clean\", [waf_light, \"clean\"])\n\n print(frame_options)\n cmd_build = [waf_light, \"build\", \"--target\", frame_options[\"waf_target\"]]\n if opts.jobs is not None:\n cmd_build += ['-j', str(opts.jobs)]\n pieces = [shlex.split(x) for x in opts.waf_build_args]\n for piece in pieces:\n cmd_build.extend(piece)\n\n _, sts = run_cmd_blocking(\"Building\", cmd_build)\n\n if sts != 0: # build failed\n if opts.rebuild_on_failure:\n progress(\"Build failed; cleaning and rebuilding\")\n run_cmd_blocking(\"Building clean\", [waf_light, \"clean\"])\n\n _, sts = run_cmd_blocking(\"Building\", cmd_build)\n if sts != 0:\n progress(\"Build failed\")\n sys.exit(1)\n else:\n progress(\"Build failed\")\n sys.exit(1)\n\n os.chdir(old_dir)\n\n\ndef do_build_parameters(vehicle):\n # build succeeded\n # now build parameters\n progress(\"Building fresh parameter descriptions\")\n param_parse_path = os.path.join(\n autotest_dir, \"param_metadata/param_parse.py\")\n cmd_param_build = [\"python\", param_parse_path, '--vehicle', vehicle]\n\n _, sts = run_cmd_blocking(\"Building fresh params\", cmd_param_build)\n if sts != 0:\n progress(\"Parameter build failed\")\n sys.exit(1)\n\n\ndef get_user_locations_path():\n '''The user locations.txt file is located by default in\n $XDG_CONFIG_DIR/ardupilot/locations.txt. If $XDG_CONFIG_DIR is\n not defined, we look in $HOME/.config/ardupilot/locations.txt. If\n $HOME is not defined, we look in ./.config/ardupilot/locations.txt.'''\n\n config_dir = os.environ.get(\n 'XDG_CONFIG_DIR',\n os.path.join(os.environ.get('HOME', '.'), '.config'))\n\n user_locations_path = os.path.join(\n config_dir, 'ardupilot', 'locations.txt')\n\n return user_locations_path\n\n\ndef find_offsets(instances, file_path):\n offsets = {}\n swarminit_filepath = os.path.join(autotest_dir, \"swarminit.txt\")\n comment_regex = re.compile(r\"\\s*#.*\")\n for path in [file_path, swarminit_filepath]:\n if os.path.isfile(path):\n with open(path, 'r') as fd:\n for line in fd:\n line = re.sub(comment_regex, \"\", line)\n line = line.rstrip(\"\\n\")\n if len(line) == 0:\n continue\n (instance, offset) = line.split(\"=\")\n instance = (int)(instance)\n if (instance not in offsets) and (instance in instances):\n offsets[instance] = [(float)(x) for x in offset.split(\",\")]\n continue\n if len(offsets) == len(instances):\n return offsets\n if len(offsets) == len(instances):\n return offsets\n for instance in instances:\n if instance not in offsets:\n offsets[instance] = [90.0, 20.0 * instance, 0.0, None]\n return offsets\n\n\ndef find_geocoder_location(locname):\n '''find a location using geocoder and SRTM'''\n try:\n import geocoder\n except ImportError:\n print(\"geocoder not installed\")\n return None\n # Step 1: Attempt the lookup\n try:\n j = geocoder.osm(locname)\n except Exception as e:\n # Handle network/blocked errors (like 403)\n err_msg = str(e)\n if '403' in err_msg:\n print(f\"geocoder access denied (HTTP 403) for '{locname}'\")\n else:\n print(f\"geocoder error: {err_msg}\")\n return None\n # Step 2: Validate the response object (Handles status_code 403 if no exception was raised)\n status_code = getattr(j, 'status_code', None)\n if status_code == 403:\n print(f\"geocoder access denied (HTTP 403) for '{locname}'\")\n return None\n\n if j is None or not hasattr(j, 'lat') or j.lat is None:\n print(f\"geocoder failed to find '{locname}'\")\n return None\n # Step 3: Success logic\n lat, lon = j.lat, j.lng\n\n from MAVProxy.modules.mavproxy_map import srtm\n downloader = srtm.SRTMDownloader()\n downloader.loadFileList()\n start = time.time()\n alt = None\n while time.time() - start &lt; 5:\n tile = downloader.getTile(int(math.floor(lat)), int(math.floor(lon)))\n if tile:\n alt = tile.getAltitudeFromLatLon(lat, lon)\n break\n if alt is None:\n print(f\"timed out getting altitude for '{locname}'\")\n return None\n return [lat, lon, alt, 0.0]\n\n\ndef find_location_by_name(locname):\n \"\"\"Search locations.txt for locname, return GPS coords\"\"\"\n locations_userpath = os.environ.get('ARDUPILOT_LOCATIONS',\n get_user_locations_path())\n locations_filepath = os.path.join(autotest_dir, \"locations.txt\")\n comment_regex = re.compile(r\"\\s*#.*\")\n for path in [locations_userpath, locations_filepath]:\n if not os.path.isfile(path):\n continue\n with open(path, 'r') as fd:\n for line in fd:\n line = re.sub(comment_regex, \"\", line)\n line = line.rstrip(\"\\n\")\n if len(line) == 0:\n continue\n (name, loc) = line.split(\"=\")\n if name == locname:\n return [(float)(x) for x in loc.split(\",\")]\n\n # fallback to geocoder if available\n loc = find_geocoder_location(locname)\n if loc is None:\n sys.exit(1)\n return loc\n\n\ndef find_spawns(loc, offsets):\n lat, lon, alt, heading = loc\n spawns = {}\n for k in offsets:\n (x, y, z, head) = offsets[k]\n if head is None:\n head = heading\n g = mavextra.gps_offset(lat, lon, x, y)\n spawns[k] = \",\".join([str(g[0]), str(g[1]), str(alt+z), str(head)])\n return spawns\n\n\ndef progress_cmd(what, cmd):\n \"\"\"Print cmd in a way a user could cut-and-paste to get the same effect\"\"\"\n progress(what)\n shell_text = \"%s\" % (\" \".join(['\"%s\"' % x for x in cmd]))\n progress(shell_text)\n\n\ndef run_cmd_blocking(what, cmd, quiet=False, check=False, **kw):\n if not quiet:\n progress_cmd(what, cmd)\n\n try:\n p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, **kw)\n ret = os.waitpid(p.pid, 0)\n except Exception as e:\n print(\"[%s] An exception has occurred with command: '%s'\" % (what, (' ').join(cmd)))\n print(e)\n sys.exit(1)\n\n _, sts = ret\n if check and sts != 0:\n progress(\"(%s) exited with code %d\" % (what, sts,))\n sys.exit(1)\n return ret\n\n\ndef run_in_terminal_window(name, cmd, **kw):\n\n \"\"\"Execute the run_in_terminal_window.sh command for cmd\"\"\"\n runme = [os.path.join(autotest_dir, \"run_in_terminal_window.sh\"), name]\n runme.extend(cmd)\n progress_cmd(\"Run \" + name, runme)\n\n if under_macos() and os.environ.get('DISPLAY'):\n # on MacOS record the window IDs so we can close them later\n out = subprocess.Popen(runme, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, **kw).communicate()[0]\n out = out.decode('utf-8')\n p = re.compile('tab 1 of window id (.*)')\n\n tstart = time.time()\n while time.time() - tstart &lt; 5:\n tabs = p.findall(out)\n\n if len(tabs) &gt; 0:\n break\n\n time.sleep(0.1)\n # sleep for extra 2 seconds for application to start\n time.sleep(2)\n if len(tabs) &gt; 0:\n windowID.append(tabs[0])\n else:\n progress(\"Cannot find %s process terminal\" % name)\n else:\n subprocess.Popen(runme, **kw)\n\n\ntracker_serial0 = None # blemish\n\n\ndef start_antenna_tracker(opts):\n \"\"\"Compile and run the AntennaTracker, add tracker to mavproxy\"\"\"\n\n global tracker_serial0\n progress(\"Preparing antenna tracker\")\n tracker_home = find_location_by_name(opts.tracker_location)\n vehicledir = os.path.join(autotest_dir, \"../../\" + \"AntennaTracker\")\n options = vinfo.options[\"AntennaTracker\"]\n tracker_default_frame = options[\"default_frame\"]\n tracker_frame_options = options[\"frames\"][tracker_default_frame]\n do_build(opts, tracker_frame_options)\n tracker_instance = 1\n oldpwd = os.getcwd()\n os.chdir(vehicledir)\n tracker_serial0 = \"tcp:127.0.0.1:\" + str(5760 + 10 * tracker_instance)\n binary_basedir = \"build/sitl\"\n exe = os.path.join(root_dir,\n binary_basedir,\n \"bin/antennatracker\")\n run_in_terminal_window(\"AntennaTracker\",\n [\"nice\",\n exe,\n \"-I\" + str(tracker_instance),\n \"--model=tracker\",\n \"--home=\" + \",\".join([str(x) for x in tracker_home])])\n os.chdir(oldpwd)\n\n\ndef start_CAN_Periph(opts, frame_info):\n \"\"\"Compile and run the sitl_periph\"\"\"\n\n progress(\"Preparing sitl_periph_universal\")\n options = vinfo.options[\"sitl_periph_universal\"]['frames']['universal']\n defaults_path = frame_info.get('periph_params_filename', None)\n if defaults_path is None:\n defaults_path = options.get('default_params_filename', None)\n\n if not isinstance(defaults_path, list):\n defaults_path = [defaults_path]\n\n #
